packages.name: Roller Conveyor

length.label: Length (m)
length.desc: Bed length along travel. Drag the dot on either end face to resize in the viewport; there is no upper limit, so one bed can stand in for a long run.

width.label: Width (m)
width.desc: Bed width across travel. Drag the dot on either side face to resize in the viewport.

speed.label: Speed (m/s, − reverses)
speed.desc: Surface speed carried along the bed. Negative runs the rollers backwards, which is the ONLY way to reverse flow - rotating the part 180 degrees moves its ends instead. A program can command this through the speed tag below.

skew.label: Roller skew (deg)
skew.desc: Angle the rollers so cargo drifts sideways as it travels and squares itself against a side guard - the standard way to align product before a merge or a labeller. The surface velocity follows the angle, and the guard does the squaring, so leave the guard on that side up.

tiltDeg.label: Incline (deg, + = head up)
tiltDeg.desc: Tilt the whole bed about its centre, positive lifting the head. This is the way to incline a roller bed - do NOT rotate the part itself, which would tip its snap ends too. Legs regrow to the floor automatically. Kept to 30 degrees because rollers shed product on a steeper grade, where a belt would hold it.

leftGuard.label: Left side guard
leftGuard.desc: Guard wall down the left side, looking along travel. This is a real barrier, so turning it off lets cargo leave the bed sideways.

rightGuard.label: Right side guard
rightGuard.desc: Guard wall down the right side, looking along travel. This is a real barrier, so turning it off lets cargo leave the bed sideways.

guardOpenings.label: Guard openings [start m, end m, side ±1/0]
guardOpenings.desc: Gaps cut in the guard wall, measured as distance ALONG the bed from the tail. Side -1 is left, +1 is right, 0 cuts both. Each gap opens the collision as well as the mesh, which is how a transfer or a diverter gets product off the lane. Press G with the bed selected to drag them in the viewport.

standHeight.label: Stand height (m)
standHeight.desc: Height of the deck above whatever is beneath it, which sets the leg length. The host fills this in when you drop or snap the conveyor, so the legs reach the floor - or a platform crossing underneath - without you measuring. Pin it by hand when you want a deliberate height.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this conveyor to the PLC. The tags below do nothing until this is on.

speedTag.label: Speed tag (REAL in: commanded speed, m/s)
speedTag.desc: The program commands surface speed here, replacing the Speed field above, which then shows the live value read-only. Careful: once BOUND this takes over even if no program drives it, and an undriven tag reads 0 - so a half-wired conveyor sits still rather than running at its authored speed.

runTag.label: Run tag (rollers run while true)
runTag.desc: Start/stop gate: false forces the speed to 0 whatever the setpoint says. Unlike the speed tag, this only takes effect once a program actually DRIVES it, so binding it alone will not stop the bed.

runningTag.label: Running tag (BOOL out: speed ≠ 0)
runningTag.desc: Feedback the conveyor publishes for the program to read: true whenever it is actually moving. This is the EFFECTIVE speed, gates included, so a run tag holding it at zero reads false here.

encoderTag.label: Encoder tag (REAL out: belt travel, m)
encoderTag.desc: Odometer of surface travel in metres, integrated on sim time and only ever climbing. Latch it when a photo-eye sees a box, then act once it has advanced a known distance - the standard way to track product without a sensor at every station.

packages.name: Box Spawner

boxesPerMinute.label: Boxes per minute
boxesPerMinute.desc: Feed rate. 0 halts the feed without disabling the part, so the timer restarts cleanly when you raise it again.

fixedRate.label: Fixed rate (off = ±50% jitter)
fixedRate.desc: On, boxes arrive on an exact metronome. Off, each gap is randomised between half and one-and-a-half times the nominal period, which is what an untidy real feed looks like downstream.

boxColor.label: Box colour
boxColor.desc: Tint for every spawned box. Ignored once the cycle list below is non-empty.

boxColors.label: Box colours (cycle, comma-sep hex)
boxColors.desc: Comma-separated hex list handed out one per box, overriding the single colour above. Useful for telling sorted lanes apart at a glance. Leave empty to use the single colour.

randomColors.label: Random colour order
randomColors.desc: Draw each colour at random from the cycle list instead of walking the list in order.

length.label: Box length (m)
length.desc: Extent along local X of each spawned box. Ignored while Random size is on.

width.label: Box width (m)
width.desc: Extent along local Z of each spawned box. Ignored while Random size is on.

height.label: Box height (m)
height.desc: Extent along local Y of each spawned box. Ignored while Random size is on.

randomSize.label: Random size
randomSize.desc: Give each box a random size and IGNORE the three dimensions above. The random range is fixed by the part (0.4-0.8 long, 0.3-0.5 high, 0.3-0.5 wide), not derived from them.

mass.label: Mass (kg)
mass.desc: Mass given to every spawned box, whatever its size.

disable.label: Disabled
disable.desc: Stop spawning entirely. The Use action toggles this in pilot mode, so it doubles as a hand stop.

conveyorId.label: Pause when conveyor stopped
conveyorId.desc: Interlock: while the named conveyor is stopped, this spawner holds. Wire that conveyor to the PLC and the feed gates itself, with no tag of its own.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The run tag below does nothing until this is on.

runTag.label: Run tag (spawn only while true)
runTag.desc: Gate the feed from the program. Note this only takes over once a program actually DRIVES the tag - until then the spawner keeps running, so a merely-declared tag is not a stopped feed.

packages.name: Diffuse Sensor

maxRange.label: Max range (m)
maxRange.desc: How far down the beam a target still counts as present. The beam is cast along local +Z, so aim the sensor by rotating it; snapping it onto a conveyor guard fits this range across the lane for you.

showBeam.label: Show beam
showBeam.desc: Draw the beam line in the viewport. A viewing aid only - hiding it does not change what the sensor detects.

normallyClosed.label: Normally closed
normallyClosed.desc: Invert the output, so the tag reads true when NOTHING is detected. The beam colour still follows the real detection, not the inverted signal.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The tag below does nothing until this is on.

tag.label: PLC tag (presence)
tag.desc: Where the photoeye publishes presence for the program to read. Whether true means blocked or clear is set by Normally closed above.

packages.name: Diverter

diverted.label: Diverted
diverted.desc: Push the blade across the lane to deflect cargo. The Use action toggles it in pilot mode; while a program drives the tag below, that program owns it instead.

divertTime.label: Divert time (s)
divertTime.desc: How long the blade takes to travel the full stroke, out or back. Too slow and cargo passes before the blade arrives.

divertDistance.label: Divert distance (m)
divertDistance.desc: How far the blade travels across the lane. Size it so the blade pushes cargo clear of the running surface rather than leaving it straddling the edge.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The tag below does nothing until this is on.

tag.label: PLC tag (bool: extend the pusher)
tag.desc: Extend the pusher from the program. While a program drives this tag it OWNS the diverter, so a hand Use in pilot mode is refused with "In auto - PLC controlled".

packages.name: Platform

length.label: Length (m)
length.desc: Deck extent along local X. Drag the dot on either end face to resize in the viewport; the frame, railing and columns reflow to match.

width.label: Width (m)
width.desc: Deck extent along local Z. Drag the dot on either side face to resize in the viewport.

height.label: Height (m)
height.desc: Height of the deck top above whatever it stands on, which is also the column length. The origin is the deck top, so raising the platform regrows the columns to reach the floor rather than leaving them hanging.

color.label: Steel color
color.desc: Steel tint of the deck, frame and columns.

showRailings.label: Perimeter railing
showRailings.desc: Guard railing around the deck edge. Turning it off removes the barrier a walking pilot leans on, not just the visual.

showSupports.label: Middle supports
showSupports.desc: Interior columns under a large deck, in addition to the corner ones. Cosmetic on a small platform, which the corners already carry.

packages.name: Blade Stop

width.label: Width (m)
width.desc: Blade width across the lane. Size it to span the conveying surface, or cargo rides past the end of the blade.

active.label: Active
active.desc: Raise the blade to stop cargo. The Use action toggles it in pilot mode; while a program drives the tag below, that program owns it instead.

raiseHeight.label: Raise height (m)
raiseHeight.desc: How far the blade top stands above the conveying surface once raised - the height of the stop cargo meets. At rest the top parks just below the surface, so raising this lengthens the stroke.

airPressureHeight.label: Air pressure height (m)
airPressureHeight.desc: Mount height of the whole moving assembly - pistons, blade and rods together - above the housing. Trim it to sit the mechanism correctly against a particular deck; it shifts the REST position, not the stroke.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The tag below does nothing until this is on.

tag.label: PLC tag (bool: raise the blade)
tag.desc: Raise the blade from the program. While a program drives this tag it OWNS the blade stop, so a hand Use in pilot mode is refused with "In auto - PLC controlled".

packages.name: Chain Transfer

chains.label: Chains
chains.desc: How many chain strands lift between the rollers. More strands spread the load, so a small or floppy carton is less likely to sag between them.

distance.label: Lane spacing (m)
distance.desc: Centre-to-centre gap between chain strands. Together with the strand count this sets how wide the transfer reaches across the host bed.

laneLength.label: Lane length (m)
laneLength.desc: How far each strand runs in the transfer direction - the stroke available to push product off the main line.

speed.label: Speed (m/s)
speed.desc: How fast the chains carry product sideways once raised. Negative sends it the other way.

raised.label: Raised (divert)
raised.desc: Lift the chains above the roller line to take the load off the main lane and drive it sideways. The Use action toggles it in pilot mode; while a program drives the pop-up tag below, that program owns it instead.

raiseTime.label: Pop-up time (s)
raiseTime.desc: How long the lift takes end to end. Treat it as a real interlock, not decoration: mid-stroke the deck is a powered surface still BELOW the roller line, dragging at the row it is about to lift, so a program must wait this out before commanding the transfer to run. There is also a floor set by the CARGO - the lift is a linear tween, so at the top the deck stops and the load does not. The default throws product about 20 mm, which a packed row survives; halve the time and it is thrown four times as far, and by about 0.07 s a row lands with its packing gone.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The tags below do nothing until this is on.

speedTag.label: Speed tag
speedTag.desc: The program commands chain speed here, replacing the Speed field above. Careful: once BOUND this takes over even if no program drives it, and an undriven tag reads 0.

popupTag.label: Pop-up tag (true = divert)
popupTag.desc: Raise the chains from the program. While a program drives this tag it OWNS the transfer, so a hand Use in pilot mode is refused with "In auto - PLC controlled".

packages.name: Shape

shape.label: Shape
shape.desc: Which primitive is built. All four are sized by the same three dimensions below, so switching kind keeps the footprint you already set.

length.label: Length X (m)
length.desc: Extent along local X, with a viewport dot on each end face. A round shape takes its X radius from half of this, so a cylinder whose length and width differ is an elliptical one.

width.label: Width Z (m)
width.desc: Extent along local Z, with a viewport dot on each side face. A round shape takes its Z radius from half of this.

height.label: Height Y (m)
height.desc: Extent along local Y. The shape is BASE-ORIGIN, sitting on local y=0, so it seats flat on the floor or a deck and grows upward.

sides.label: Sides
sides.desc: How many facets go around a cylinder or cone. No effect on a box or a ramp.

solid.label: Solid (blocks cargo)
solid.desc: Give the shape a collision hull, so cargo and a walking pilot are stopped by it. The hull is exact for all four shapes, which is what lets a ramp actually be walked up rather than colliding as a full block. Clear it for pure massing or decoration.

packages.name: Push Button

text.label: Face label
text.desc: Text rendered onto the cap. Keep it short enough to read at station distance.

buttonColor.label: Button color
buttonColor.desc: Tint of the cap, and of the lamp when it lights.

momentary.label: Momentary (else maintained latch)
momentary.desc: On, each press is a fixed 0.3 s pulse of sim time, like a spring-return start button - so a paused sim holds the pulse rather than letting it expire. Off, the button latches on one press and releases on the next, like a maintained selector.

normallyClosed.label: Normally closed (invert output)
normallyClosed.desc: Invert the output, so the tag reads true while the button is NOT pressed - the safety convention for a stop button, where a broken wire reads the same as a press.

lampSource.label: Lamp source
lampSource.desc: What lights the cap. Follows press echoes this button, the way a contact strapped to the light block would. PLC tag hands the lamp to the program through Lamp tag below - the acknowledge wiring a real panel uses. Always on is a power-on indicator. Unlit is a button with no light block fitted.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The tags below do nothing until this is on.

tag.label: PLC tag (button output)
tag.desc: Where the button publishes its press for the program to read. Whether true means pressed or at-rest is set by Normally closed above.

lampTag.label: Lamp tag (bool: PLC lights the cap)
lampTag.desc: Which PLC bool lights the cap, so the program can acknowledge a press rather than just echo it. Read only when Lamp source above is set to PLC tag; left unbound there, the lamp stays dark like an unwired light block.

packages.name: Stack Light

segments.label: Segments
segments.desc: How many lamp tiers are stacked. Colours are fixed and cycle bottom-up: green, amber, red, blue, white.

value.label: Value (bitmask)
value.desc: Which tiers are lit, as a bitmask: bit 0 is the BOTTOM tier, so 1 lights green, 2 lights amber, 3 lights both. Bits above the segment count are masked off. A program driving the tag below replaces this value.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The tag below does nothing until this is on.

tag.label: PLC tag (int bitmask)
tag.desc: The program writes the lit-tier bitmask here. While it drives the tag it OWNS the light, so the Value field above becomes a read-only readout and a hand Use is refused with "In auto - PLC controlled".

packages.name: Six-Axis Robot

speed.label: Joint speed (°/s)
speed.desc: Top speed along the joint-space path. All six joints are driven from one path parameter, so they start and arrive together instead of the fastest one finishing early.

accel.label: Joint accel (°/s²)
accel.desc: How hard the arm ramps to and from the joint speed. Lower it for a heavier or more delicate payload; a short move may never reach top speed at all.

scale.label: Scale
scale.desc: Uniform size multiplier on the whole robot, applied to its collision bodies as well as its appearance - so a scaled arm really does reach further, rather than just looking bigger.

toolSizeX.label: Tool size X (m)
toolSizeX.desc: Length of the vacuum plate. The orange dots on the tool itself drag this in the viewport, and they ride the arm, so you can size the tool in whatever pose you are inspecting. Size it to the product you are picking - the plate is also the grab reach.

toolSizeZ.label: Tool size Z (m)
toolSizeZ.desc: Width of the vacuum plate, dragged by the same orange dots on the tool.

cupPitchX.label: Cup pitch X (m)
cupPitchX.desc: Centre-to-centre spacing of the suction cups along the plate length. The plate fits as many as the pitch allows, so tightening it adds cups rather than moving them.

cupPitchZ.label: Cup pitch Z (m)
cupPitchZ.desc: Centre-to-centre spacing of the suction cups across the plate width.

cupMarginX.label: Cup margin X (m)
cupMarginX.desc: Inset from each end of the plate before the first cup, so the grid does not run off the edge.

cupMarginZ.label: Cup margin Z (m)
cupMarginZ.desc: Inset from each side of the plate before the first cup.

cupsEnabled.label: Suction cups
cupsEnabled.desc: Draw the cup grid under the plate. Appearance only - the grip itself comes from the vacuum tag, not from the cups being visible.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this robot to the PLC. The tags below do nothing until this is on, and without them the arm just rests at its idle pose.

commandTag.label: Command tag (INT: 0=home, 1+=waypoint)
commandTag.desc: Which row of the waypoint table to move to, as an index: 0 is home, 1 the second row and so on. Set it BEFORE pulsing execute. An index past the end of the table is ignored, and the arm stays put rather than guessing.

executeTag.label: Execute tag (rising edge runs the move)
executeTag.desc: Pulse this false-to-true to start the move. It is edge-triggered, so holding it true does NOT repeat - drop it and raise it again for each move.

doneTag.label: Done tag (true while idle)
doneTag.desc: Handshake back to the program: true whenever the arm is parked and ready for the next command. Wait for it before pulsing execute again, or the edge lands mid-move and is dropped.

gripperTag.label: Vacuum tag
gripperTag.desc: Grip or release the load. Read continuously rather than on an edge, so hold it true for the whole carry and drop it only once the load is where it belongs.

waypoints.label: Waypoints ([j1..j6 °]; row 0 = home)
waypoints.desc: The poses this robot knows, one row of six JOINT angles each - not a position in space, so the arm reaches a pose exactly as taught with no ambiguity about elbow or wrist. Row 0 is home, and the command tag indexes into this table. Pose the arm with the viewport gizmo and use Capture Pose to append the row rather than typing angles.

blendWaypoints.label: Blend-through waypoint indices (corner without stopping)
blendWaypoints.desc: Which waypoint indices are VIA points: the arm corners through these carrying its speed instead of braking to a stop, which is what turns a jerky index-and-stop cycle into one flowing motion. Leave pick and place poses OUT of this list - those have to arrive exactly.

blendDeg.label: Corner blend (° before a via-point to hand off)
blendDeg.desc: How early the arm starts cutting the corner at a via point. Larger rounds the path more and moves it further from the taught pose; the arm also caps it at a third of the current move, so a short leg blends less than you asked for rather than overshooting.

pose.label: Idle pose ([j1..j6 °])
pose.desc: The pose a freshly placed robot rests in, and where one waiting for its first Execute sits. It is the arm you see in a stopped scene, so set it to something that reads as parked rather than mid-cycle.

packages.name: Pallet

mass.label: Mass (kg)
mass.desc: Physical mass of the pallet itself, before anything is stacked on it.

color.label: Color
color.desc: Tint over the pallet wood texture. White leaves it untinted.

packages.name: Box

length.label: Length (m)
length.desc: Extent along local X. Drives the collision body as well as the visual, and the box is centred on its origin.

height.label: Height (m)
height.desc: Extent along local Y. Drives the collision body as well as the visual.

width.label: Width (m)
width.desc: Extent along local Z. Drives the collision body as well as the visual.

mass.label: Mass (kg)
mass.desc: Physical mass. Heavier cargo is harder for a conveyor to accelerate and pushes lighter cargo out of the way.

color.label: Color
color.desc: Tint over the cardboard texture. White leaves it untinted.

packages.name: Pallet Spawner

palletsPerMinute.label: Pallets per minute
palletsPerMinute.desc: Feed rate. 0 halts the magazine without disabling the part.

fixedRate.label: Fixed rate (off = ±50% jitter)
fixedRate.desc: On, pallets arrive on an exact metronome. Off, each gap is randomised between half and one-and-a-half times the nominal period.

palletColor.label: Pallet colour
palletColor.desc: Tint multiplied over the pallet wood model. Leave it white unless you want dispensed pallets to read differently from hand-placed ones beside them.

mass.label: Mass (kg)
mass.desc: Mass given to every dispensed pallet, before anything is stacked on it.

disable.label: Disabled
disable.desc: Stop dispensing entirely. The Use action toggles this in pilot mode, so it doubles as a hand stop.

conveyorId.label: Pause when conveyor stopped
conveyorId.desc: Interlock: while the named conveyor is stopped, this spawner holds. Wire that conveyor to the PLC and the feed gates itself, with no tag of its own.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The run tag below does nothing until this is on.

runTag.label: Run tag (spawn only while true)
runTag.desc: Gate the magazine from the program. Note this only takes over once a program actually DRIVES the tag - until then the spawner keeps running, so a merely-declared tag is not a stopped feed.

packages.name: Fence

length.label: Length (m)
length.desc: Fence run length along local +X. Drag the dot on either end face to resize in the viewport; short runs are legitimate filler panels where a guard line meets a machine.

height.label: Height (m)
height.desc: Panel height. The base stays on the floor and the top face moves, so the viewport dot drags the top.

meshColor.label: Mesh color
meshColor.desc: Tint of the frame and the wire panel it holds.

omitPostStart.label: Omit start post
omitPostStart.desc: Suppress the post at local -X so a snapped neighbour draws the shared one instead. Snapping sets this for you.

omitPostEnd.label: Omit end post
omitPostEnd.desc: Suppress the post at local +X so a snapped neighbour draws the shared one instead. Snapping sets this for you.

packages.name: Safety Gate

length.label: Width (m)
length.desc: Gate width, hinge post to latch post. Size it to the gap you are closing in the fence line.

open.label: Open
open.desc: Swing the leaf open. The Use action toggles it in pilot mode, which is how someone walks through the guard line.

openAngle.label: Open angle (°)
openAngle.desc: How far the leaf swings about the hinge when open. Negative angles swing it the other way, for a gate that has to open into the aisle.

openSpeed.label: Open speed (°/s)
openSpeed.desc: How fast the leaf travels between shut and the open angle.

normallyClosed.label: Normally closed (invert signal)
normallyClosed.desc: Invert the signal this gate publishes, so the tag reads true while the gate is SHUT - the safety convention, where a broken wire and an open gate look the same to the program. Affects the comms output only, never the visuals.

meshColor.label: Mesh color
meshColor.desc: Tint of the leaf frame and the panel it holds.

handleColor.label: Handle color
handleColor.desc: Tint of the emergency release handle.

omitPostStart.label: Omit start post
omitPostStart.desc: Suppress the post at local -X so a snapped neighbour draws the shared one instead. Snapping sets this for you.

omitPostEnd.label: Omit end post
omitPostEnd.desc: Suppress the post at local +X so a snapped neighbour draws the shared one instead. Snapping sets this for you.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The tag below does nothing until this is on.

tag.label: PLC tag (bool: gate signal out)
tag.desc: Where the gate publishes its state for the program to read. Whether true means open or shut is set by Normally closed above.

packages.name: Floor Marking

length.label: Length (m)
length.desc: Extent along local X. Drag the dot on either end face to resize in the viewport.

width.label: Width (m)
width.desc: Extent along local Z. Drag the dot on either side face to resize in the viewport.

style.label: Style
style.desc: Which pattern is painted into the rectangle. Border draws an outline only and leaves the interior bare floor; every other style covers the whole footprint.

stripeSize.label: Stripe size (m)
stripeSize.desc: Width of one stripe or dash (the pattern repeats every two of them). Bands are phased from this part's own origin, so two markings laid end to end won't necessarily line up.

borderWidth.label: Border width (m)
borderWidth.desc: Width of the border band. Only the Border style draws one.

primaryColor.label: Primary color
primaryColor.desc: The base colour: the solid fill, the first hazard/stripe band, the dashed field, the border itself. Always painted, and always opaque - the bands are geometry, so partial alpha does nothing here.

secondaryColor.label: Secondary color
secondaryColor.desc: The alternating colour: the second hazard/stripe band and the dashes. Take its alpha all the way to zero to drop those bands entirely and leave bare floor between the primary ones; any other alpha paints opaque. Unused by Solid and Border.

packages.name: Turntable Conveyor

width.label: Lane width (m)
width.desc: Width of the conveying lane across the deck. Size it to the conveyors it indexes between, since the lane is what actually carries product once the deck has settled.

standHeight.label: Stand height (m)
standHeight.desc: Height of the deck above whatever is beneath it, which sets the leg length. The host fills this in when you drop or snap the turntable, so raising it regrows the legs to reach.

speed.label: Speed (m/s)
speed.desc: How fast the lane conveys once the deck has SETTLED at its target angle. While the deck is still slewing the lane carries nothing forward - product just rides round with the platter - so this only applies between moves.

deckAngleDeg.label: Deck angle (°)
deckAngleDeg.desc: Target angle for the deck, which then slews to it and holds. This is the whole control surface when comms are off: an angled cross-feed you aim from the Inspector rather than a self-runner. A program commands it through the angle tag below instead.

rotationSpeedDeg.label: Rotation speed (°/s, top)
rotationSpeedDeg.desc: TOP slew rate, reached through a fixed acceleration ramp rather than instantly. The default indexes 90 degrees in about 5 seconds including both ramps, which is where real units sit - winding it much higher asks more of the deck than a real drive delivers, and product slides.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this part to the PLC. The tags below do nothing until this is on.

angleTag.label: Target-angle tag (REAL °)
angleTag.desc: The program commands the deck angle here, replacing the Deck angle field above. On the first scan the part SEEDS the tag with the authored angle, so a program that has not written yet does not slam the deck to zero.

speedTag.label: Speed tag (REAL m/s)
speedTag.desc: The program commands lane speed here, replacing the Speed field above. Careful: once BOUND this takes over even if no program drives it, and an undriven tag reads 0.

doneTag.label: Done tag (true once settled)
doneTag.desc: Handshake back to the program: true once the deck has stopped at its target angle. Wait on this before commanding the lane to run, or product is pushed at a deck still turning under it.

packages.name: AGV

driveSpeed.label: Drive speed (m/s)
driveSpeed.desc: How fast the truck travels between waypoints.

turnSpeed.label: Turn speed (°/s)
turnSpeed.desc: How fast it pivots on the spot. Every move turns to face the target, drives, then turns to the waypoint heading, so this sets much of the cycle time on short hops.

liftSpeed.label: Fork lift speed (m/s)
liftSpeed.desc: How fast the tines raise and lower to the height the waypoint asks for.

maxLiftHeight.label: Max fork height (m)
maxLiftHeight.desc: Ceiling on the tines, whatever a waypoint asks for. Set it to the top beam of the racking the truck actually serves.

reverseRange.label: Back-out range (m; 0 = always turn)
reverseRange.desc: How close a target has to be for the truck to REVERSE to it instead of turning round. It only applies when the target is behind, within this range, and at roughly the heading already held - the shape of withdrawing tines from a rack bay, where turning would swing two metres of fork through the uprights. Set 0 to always turn and drive forward.

enableComms.label: Enable comms
enableComms.desc: Expose this truck to the PLC. The tags below do nothing until this is on, and without them the truck simply parks at home.

commandTag.label: Command tag (INT: 0=home, 1+=waypoint)
commandTag.desc: Which row of the waypoint table to drive to, as an index: 0 is home, 1 the second row and so on. Set it BEFORE pulsing execute. An index past the end of the table is ignored, and the truck stays put rather than guessing.

executeTag.label: Execute tag (rising edge runs the move)
executeTag.desc: Pulse this false-to-true to start the move. It is edge-triggered, so holding it true does NOT repeat - drop it and raise it again for each move. An edge arriving mid-move is ignored.

doneTag.label: Done tag (true while idle)
doneTag.desc: Handshake back to the program: true whenever the truck is parked and ready for the next command. Wait for it before pulsing execute again, or the edge lands mid-move and is dropped.

forkTag.label: Fork tag (true grabs, false releases)
forkTag.desc: Clamp or release whatever is sitting on the tines. It is read continuously rather than on an edge, so hold it true for the whole carry and drop it only once the load is where it belongs.

waypoints.label: Waypoints ([x, z, °, fork height m]; row 0 = home)
waypoints.desc: The stops this truck knows, one row each: where to stand in scene X and Z, which way to face, and how high to carry the tines. Row 0 is home, and the command tag indexes into this table - so adding a row is how the program gets somewhere new to send it.

packages.name: Rack

length.label: Width (m)
length.desc: Frame width along local X. Drag the dot on either end face to resize in the viewport; while auto poles are on that drag snaps to whole bays, so the rack always ends on an upright.

depth.label: Depth (m)
depth.desc: Frame depth along local Z. Drag the dot on either side face to resize in the viewport.

numShelves.label: Shelves
numShelves.desc: How many shelf levels sit above the floor. With the spacing below, this is what sets the total height.

shelfSpacing.label: Shelf spacing (m)
shelfSpacing.desc: Vertical gap between shelf levels. Leave room for the tallest load you mean to store, plus the truck reaching it.

enableAutoPoles.label: Auto poles
enableAutoPoles.desc: Fill the footprint with a grid of uprights and load beams. Off leaves four corner posts only, which reads as a light shelving unit rather than pallet racking.

poleInterval.label: Pole interval (m)
poleInterval.desc: Centre-to-centre spacing of the uprights, applied along both width and depth. This is also the bay size a viewport resize snaps to.

frameColor.label: Frame color
frameColor.desc: Tint of the uprights and load beams.

packages.name: Stairs

numSteps.label: Steps
numSteps.desc: Number of steps in the flight, which is what sets both its rise and its run: the slope is fixed at the standard 0.178 m rise over a 0.28 m tread, so a flight grows along the diagonal rather than getting steeper. Count the steps you need to reach the deck.

showHandrails.label: Handrails
showHandrails.desc: Handrails up both sides of the flight.

color.label: Steel color
color.desc: Steel tint of the treads, stringers and rails.
